back.body: GENERIC NAME — the OFFICIAL name of the drug itself; lower case, SAME EVERYWHERE · TRADE NAME — a manufacturer's BRAND name; capitalised, and ONE DRUG MAY HAVE MANY · CHEMICAL NAME — the molecule; of no practical use to you · PATIENTS KNOW TRADE NAMES AND NOT GENERIC ONES, because that is what is on the box · TWO BOXES WITH DIFFERENT TRADE NAMES CAN HOLD THE SAME DRUG — a real cause of DOUBLE DOSING, and a reason to bring the boxes · FORM DETERMINES ROUTE, SPEED AND WHETHER THIS PATIENT CAN TAKE IT: tablets · capsules · liquids · gels · sprays · inhalers · auto-injectors · AND COMPRESSED GAS — OXYGEN IS A DRUG · WRITE DOWN EXACTLY WHAT IS ON THE BOX, not what you think it means
back.why_it_matters: Same drug. He had been taking it twice a day for about three weeks.

front.title: Routes
front.summary: Closer and better supplied means faster

back.body: ROUTE DECIDES HOW FAST IT WORKS AND HOW MUCH REACHES THE BLOOD · THE PRINCIPLE: THE CLOSER TO THE BLOODSTREAM AND THE BETTER THE BLOOD SUPPLY, THE FASTER · ORAL — SLOWEST: gut absorption, then the liver · NEVER GIVE ANYTHING BY MOUTH TO A PATIENT WHO CANNOT PROTECT THEIR AIRWAY. That question comes BEFORE every other consideration · SUBLINGUAL — rich blood supply, thin lining, FAST, and BYPASSES THE GUT AND LIVER. Does not work in a dry mouth · INHALED — fast, and puts the drug WHERE THE LUNG PROBLEM IS · INTRAMUSCULAR — reliable, no vein, basic training: why AUTO-INJECTORS use it · INTRANASAL — fast, no needle, works on the uncooperative · INTRAVENOUS — fastest and most complete; outside EMT scope in most systems · MATCH THE ROUTE TO THE PATIENT, not to the drug in the abstract
back.why_it_matters: The question is not whether the drug is right. It is whether this patient can protect their airway.

back.body: A DRUG CHANGES SOMETHING THE BODY ALREADY DOES — speeds it up, slows it down, or BLOCKS it · ONSET (how long until it works, HEAVILY ROUTE-DEPENDENT) · PEAK · DURATION · HALF-LIFE (time to remove half of it) · AGONIST PRODUCES an effect · ANTAGONIST BLOCKS one, and some reverse overdoses · AN ANTAGONIST CAN WEAR OFF BEFORE THE DRUG IT REVERSED — SO THE ORIGINAL EFFECT CAN COME BACK. A REVERSED PATIENT STILL NEEDS TRANSPORT AND WATCHING, however well they look · ABSORPTION · DISTRIBUTION · METABOLISM (liver) · ELIMINATION (kidneys) — which is why OLDER AND UNWELL PATIENTS ACCUMULATE DRUGS and react more strongly · TOLERANCE: more needed over time for the same effect · ALWAYS REASSESS AFTER GIVING — what happened matters, not what should have
back.why_it_matters: He went, on that sentence rather than on any argument about authority.

back.body: INDICATION — the reason TO give it · CONTRAINDICATION — a reason NOT to, because here it would HARM · INDICATIONS ARE OBVIOUS; CONTRAINDICATIONS HIDE IN THE HISTORY, which is why one needs ACTIVE CHECKING · ABSOLUTE = never in this situation · RELATIVE = weigh it, usually with medical direction · SIDE EFFECTS are other effects, MOSTLY PREDICTABLE FROM THE MECHANISM · ADVERSE EFFECTS are harmful — LOOK FOR THEM, do not wait to notice · ALLERGY IS NOT A SIDE EFFECT: nausea is a side effect; RASH, SWELLING, WHEEZE, DIFFICULTY BREATHING is allergy · BUT ON SCENE: REPORTED ALLERGY MEANS YOU DO NOT GIVE IT — sorting it out is a hospital conversation · ASK ABOUT ALLERGIES BEFORE EVERY ADMINISTRATION, INCLUDING REPEATS · OTHER MEDICATIONS CAN CREATE A CONTRAINDICATION NEITHER DRUG HAS ALONE · UNSURE? CONTACT MEDICAL DIRECTION
back.why_it_matters: It felt slightly ridiculous and they asked it anyway. The answer had changed.

back.body: A CHECKLIST RUN BEFORE EVERY SINGLE ADMINISTRATION — and being able to LIST them is not the skill; RUNNING them at 3am when you are tired is · RIGHT PATIENT · RIGHT MEDICATION (READ THE LABEL, at the moment you open it, not from memory or shelf position) · RIGHT DOSE (amount AND CONCENTRATION — the same drug often comes in more than one) · RIGHT ROUTE · RIGHT TIME (HAS A DOSE ALREADY BEEN GIVEN? by the patient, family, first responders, your own crew — ASK) · RIGHT DOCUMENTATION (what, how much, route, time, who, AND THE EFFECT) · READ THE LABEL THREE TIMES: picking up, preparing, before it goes in · SAY THE CHECKS OUT LOUD — silent checking FEELS IDENTICAL AND IS WORSE · THE DANGER IS FAMILIARITY
back.why_it_matters: The partner said, without looking up, that the concentration was not the usual one.

back.body: 1 RIGHT PATIENT · 2 RIGHT MEDICATION — READ THE LABEL · 3 RIGHT DOSE — amount AND CONCENTRATION · 4 RIGHT ROUTE · 5 RIGHT TIME — has a dose already been given? · 6 RIGHT DOCUMENTATION — including THE EFFECT · HABIT ONE: READ THE LABEL THREE TIMES · HABIT TWO: SAY THE CHECKS OUT LOUD · Some programmes add a seventh right — follow your own version · THE REAL DANGER IS FAMILIARITY.
back.why_it_matters: The number matters less than the fact that you actually perform them.

back.body: ERRORS HAPPEN TO CAREFUL, COMPETENT, EXPERIENCED PEOPLE — that is the ASSUMPTION THE WHOLE CHECKING SYSTEM IS BUILT ON · COMMON: wrong drug · wrong dose · wrong route · wrong patient · A DOSE GIVEN TWICE because each thought the other had not · KNOWN CAUSES: LOOK-ALIKE PACKAGING · SOUND-ALIKE NAMES · DISTRACTION OR INTERRUPTION DURING PREPARATION, one of the strongest associations there is · IF IT HAPPENS: 1. CARE FOR THE PATIENT — not investigate, not explain · 2. TELL YOUR PARTNER, MEDICAL DIRECTION AND THE HOSPITAL IMMEDIATELY — their treatment depends on knowing what is actually in the patient · 3. DOCUMENT WHAT WAS ACTUALLY GIVEN, INCLUDING THE ERROR · NEVER CONCEAL AND NEVER ALTER THE RECORD · REPORT NEAR MISSES TOO
back.why_it_matters: She said give me ten seconds, finished, read the label again, and then answered.

back.body: YOUR PROTOCOL AND MEDICAL DIRECTOR DECIDE WHAT YOU MAY GIVE — not what you know, not what would obviously help, not what you did elsewhere · ADMINISTER = your service's medication under your own authority · ASSIST = helping a patient with THEIR OWN PRESCRIBED medication — a DIFFERENT authority, usually with conditions (prescribed to them, in date, criteria met) · STANDING ORDERS (offline) = written pre-authorisation; THE DECISION IS ALREADY MADE · ONLINE = a physician order for THIS patient, NOW · KNOW WHICH IS WHICH BEFORE YOU NEED TO · GIVE A CLEAR ORDERED PICTURE, THEN REPEAT THE ORDER BACK — three seconds, noisy radios, similar-sounding names · IF AN ORDER SEEMS UNSAFE, SAY THE SPECIFIC FINDING AND ASK FOR CONFIRMATION — you are the one in the room · ACTING OUTSIDE SCOPE IS SERIOUS EVEN WHEN YOU WERE RIGHT
back.why_it_matters: The order changed. The physician had not had that piece of information.

back.body: OXYGEN IS A DRUG — indications, contraindications, effects and harms like anything else · INDICATED where the patient is HYPOXIC or where HYPOXIA IS LIKELY given the presentation — you do not always have a number first · MORE IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY BETTER: the aim is ADEQUATE OXYGENATION, NOT MAXIMUM DELIVERY, and excess is harmful in some conditions. TARGET PER PROTOCOL · DEVICE FOLLOWS NEED: cannula (lower) · non-rebreather (high) · BAG-VALVE-MASK where breathing is INADEQUATE — that patient needs SOMEONE TO MOVE AIR FOR THEM, not a richer mixture · OXYGEN DOES NOT BURN; IT MAKES EVERYTHING ELSE BURN FASTER — a real fire hazard, and SAY IT OUT LOUD to family who smoke · CYLINDERS ARE HIGH PRESSURE — a damaged valve is a projectile · DURATION AND DEVICE DETAIL LIVE IN MODULE 02
back.why_it_matters: He had genuinely not thought about it, which is the usual answer.

back.body: GIVEN FOR SUSPECTED LOW BLOOD SUGAR — and one of the most satisfying things an EMT does · THE PATIENT MUST BE ABLE TO SWALLOW AND PROTECT THEIR OWN AIRWAY. That governs everything else · AND HERE IS THE TRAP: LOW SUGAR PRODUCES EXACTLY THE PATIENTS IN WHOM THAT IS UNCERTAIN — drowsy, confused, intermittently responsive. The indication and the danger arrive in the SAME PATIENT · NEVER TO AN UNCONSCIOUS PATIENT: not a smear, not on the gums, not because the family says it usually works · PLACE BETWEEN THE CHEEK AND THE GUM, not deep in the mouth · REASSESS — improvement is usually within MINUTES; document before and after · NO IMPROVEMENT MEANS THINK AGAIN, NOT GIVE MORE: stroke, head injury, overdose, hypoxia, infection
back.why_it_matters: This might be the right drug for the wrong problem. Saying it early started everything else.

back.body: A HEART ATTACK IS A CLOT BLOCKING A CORONARY ARTERY · PLATELETS START THE CLOT; ASPIRIN MAKES THEM LESS ABLE TO STICK TOGETHER, LIMITING IT · SO IT IS NOT TREATING THE PAIN — IT IS ACTING ON THE MECHANISM OF THE DISEASE · IT IS ONE OF VERY FEW PREHOSPITAL ACTIONS IN HEART ATTACK WITH CLEAR EVIDENCE OF BENEFIT · GIVE IT EARLY — the benefit is greatest BEFORE the clot is established, it takes seconds and needs no equipment, so it belongs at the FRONT of the call · CHEWED, not swallowed whole, where protocol directs · CONTRAINDICATIONS: known ALLERGY · ACTIVE BLEEDING · per protocol · cannot protect the airway · ASK WHETHER THEY HAVE ALREADY TAKEN IT TODAY — many take it daily, and some take one at onset, and nobody volunteers it · NOT GIVEN TO CHILDREN FOR FEVER
back.why_it_matters: He had taken one two hours earlier, because that is what he had been told to do.

back.body: DILATES VESSELS → LESS WORK FOR THE HEART → LESS OXYGEN DEMAND → the pain eases · AT EMT LEVEL THIS IS USUALLY ASSISTING WITH THE PATIENT'S OWN PRESCRIPTION — prescribed to them, in date, protocol criteria met · SUBLINGUAL tablet or spray — fast, bypasses the gut and liver · EVERY DANGER FOLLOWS FROM ONE PROPERTY: IT LOWERS BLOOD PRESSURE · SYSTOLIC BELOW YOUR PROTOCOL'S THRESHOLD — contraindicated · ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION MEDICATION within your protocol's period — THE COMBINATION CAN DROP PRESSURE CATASTROPHICALLY AND HAS KILLED PEOPLE. ASK, PRIVATELY, MATTER-OF-FACTLY · HEAD INJURY · MAXIMUM DOSES PER PROTOCOL · BLOOD PRESSURE BEFORE EACH DOSE AND AFTER, EVERY TIME · WARN ABOUT HEADACHE · SIT OR LIE THEM DOWN — fainting is real · FULL LIST WITH FIGURES: EMT-04-02-08
back.why_it_matters: Somebody asked the family to fetch his list from upstairs, and then asked it.

back.body: EPINEPHRINE IS THE TREATMENT FOR ANAPHYLAXIS — not one of them, THE one · IT OPENS THE AIRWAYS, TIGHTENS THE VESSELS AND SUPPORTS THE PRESSURE AT THE SAME TIME, which is why nothing substitutes for it · THE COMMONEST ERROR IS GIVING IT TOO LATE — not wrongly, not too much. TOO LATE. Deaths in anaphylaxis are associated with the minutes spent being careful · IN TRUE ANAPHYLAXIS THERE IS NO ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION — a cardiac history is not a reason to withhold it · INTRAMUSCULAR, OUTER THIGH, THROUGH CLOTHING — by design · HOLD FOR THE DEVICE'S TIME, THEN NOTE THE TIME · THUMB CLEAR OF BOTH ENDS — injecting your own thumb removes a provider from the call · IT WEARS OFF: a second dose may be needed · EVERY PATIENT IS TRANSPORTED
back.why_it_matters: The partner said one word, which was now, and gave it.

back.body: RELAXES THE MUSCLE AROUND THE AIRWAYS, opening them · At EMT level usually ASSISTING WITH THE PATIENT'S OWN INHALER — prescribed to them, in date, protocol criteria met · TECHNIQUE IS WHERE THE DOSE IS LOST: a badly used inhaler puts most of it ON THE BACK OF THE THROAT · SHAKE → BREATHE OUT → SEAL → FIRE AT THE START OF A SLOW DEEP BREATH IN → HOLD BRIEFLY. THE COORDINATION IS THE WHOLE TRICK · A SPACER IMPROVES DELIVERY CONSIDERABLY — many patients own one and have left it in a drawer. ASK · FAST HEART RATE, TREMOR AND JITTERINESS ARE EXPECTED — warn them, or they will think they are getting worse · REASSESS BY LISTENING AND BY WORK OF BREATHING, not by asking · A PATIENT TOO EXHAUSTED TO BREATHE IN DEEPLY CANNOT USE ONE — ESCALATE, do not repeat
back.why_it_matters: The next dose actually went where it was supposed to.

back.body: BLOCKS THE RECEPTORS THE OPIOID IS ACTING ON · OPIOID OVERDOSE KILLS BY STOPPING BREATHING — they are not dying of being unconscious · SO WHERE BREATHING IS INADEQUATE, VENTILATE FIRST, THEN GIVE IT · INTRANASAL OR INTRAMUSCULAR at EMT level — neither needs a vein · AIM FOR ADEQUATE BREATHING, NOT A FULLY AWAKE PATIENT. Breathing well but drowsy IS A SUCCESS · NALOXONE CAN WEAR OFF BEFORE THE OPIOID DOES — SO EVERY PATIENT IS TRANSPORTED AND WATCHED, however well they look. 'WHAT WOKE YOU UP WILL WEAR OFF BEFORE WHAT PUT YOU DOWN' · EXPECT WITHDRAWAL IN DEPENDENT PATIENTS: nausea, vomiting, pain, AGITATION — A DRUG EFFECT, NOT BAD BEHAVIOUR. Stand clear, have suction ready, explain calmly · NO RESPONSE? RECONSIDER THE DIAGNOSIS
back.why_it_matters: By the time it went in, the patient had been oxygenated for two minutes rather than reversed while blue.

back.body: BINDS CERTAIN SWALLOWED POISONS IN THE GUT so less is absorbed — the charcoal itself passes straight through · THREE LIMITS: IT DOES NOT BIND EVERYTHING · IT IS TIME-CRITICAL, and the benefit falls away as the poison is absorbed · MANY SYSTEMS NO LONGER CARRY IT, AND MANY REQUIRE MEDICAL DIRECTION — FIND OUT WHAT YOURS DOES · THE PATIENT MUST BE ALERT ENOUGH TO SWALLOW AND PROTECT THEIR AIRWAY, and here it is ABSOLUTE: ASPIRATED CHARCOAL CAUSES SEVERE LUNG INJURY · POISONED PATIENTS FLUCTUATE — ASK WHAT THEY WILL BE LIKE IN TEN MINUTES, NOT JUST NOW · CONTRAINDICATED AFTER CORROSIVES (no benefit, and it hides the damaged tissue) AND PETROLEUM PRODUCTS (aspiration on vomiting) · IT IS GENUINELY UNPLEASANT — SAY SO HONESTLY · USE POISON CONTROL
back.why_it_matters: What is she likely to be in ten minutes, given what she took and when?
